summary: Contractual rate override not honored during private -> hosted fallback resulting in unexpected invoice line
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Kestrel Health reports that a contractual rate override (enterprise addendum ID: KH-2025-A) is not being applied when their private deployment falls back to hosted in eu-west. They were charged at standard hosted per-token rates for ~3 hours on 2026-03-09 during a private->hosted fallback window.

Impact:
- Unexpected invoice line of ~€18,564 for fallback-hosted usage on the March invoice.
- Affects revenue recognition and customer expectations (enterprise contract explicitly specifies a lowered hosted fallback rate for private customers).
- Customer-facing SLA and CSM escalation opened; finance has paused autopay pending resolution.

Environment:
- Customer: Kestrel Health (private deployment, enterprise tier)
- Private control plane: vpc-kestrel-eu (managed by Redwood Private)
- Fallback path: private -> hosted (eu-west) automatic routing when private pool under capacity pressure
- Time window: 2026-03-09 02:12:00 to 2026-03-09 05:29:00 UTC
- Affected model: redwood-open-7b-v2 (pinned in customer config)

Steps to reproduce / observed workflow:
1) Simulated load test ran by customer at 02:10 UTC; private pool reached 98% GPU utilization.
2) Smart routing triggered fallback policy to hosted (eu-west) as expected.
3) Requests successfully executed on hosted; however billing records attribute usage to standard hosted tariff without KH-2025-A override.
4) Customer observed invoice charge for hosted usage and raised ticket via CSM.

Logs / evidence attached:
- Routing audit (s3://billing-audit/eu-west/2026-03-09/routing-20260309-02-05.log) [link redacted for support]
- Billing postbacks showing per-token rate applied (billing-id: bill-eu-20260309-459)
- Contract snippet uploaded to ticket (KH-2025-A clause 4.2 fallback-rate = 0.0045 EUR/token)
- Console screenshot: per-route cost breakdown for the fallback window

Initial hypothesis (Support):
- Rate override lookup was not applied for fallback-attributed postbacks because of an ordering issue in the rate-lookup service: the private-rate check happens in the routing phase but billing postback is evaluated against hosted-tariff by default when origin=hosted.
- Another possibility: the customer’s enterprise metadata tag (contract_id: KH-2025-A) was not present on hosted-side postbacks due to a header stripping in proxying.

Work done so far (investigation notes):
- Support retrieved routing audit and confirmed requests did hit hosted endpoints (confirmed).
- Billing team inspected the postback and found contract_id missing on ~72% of the postbacks during the window; remaining 28% included contract_id but still had standard tariff (inconsistent behavior).
- Routing engineers reproduced a local scenario using the private->hosted shim; observed that X-Redwood-Contract header is forwarded from private router, but our hosted ingress removes unknown headers as part of the proxy hardening rule set.
- Eng confirmed a recent proxy hardening change (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/214) added header whitelist; contract metadata must be present in the request body for billing to pick it up.

Proposed next steps / mitigation plan:
1) Immediate: apply provisional credit for the disputed hosted-line amount (finance approval requested) so customer invoice can be corrected while root-cause is fixed. (Assigned to Billing: Carlos Mendes)
2) Short term (hotfix): update hosted billing postback processor to fall back to routing tags (routing-audit correlation) when contract_id header absent. (Assigned to Billing + Routing)
3) Medium term: change proxy hardening whitelist to include X-Redwood-Contract and ensure the private->hosted shim preserves contract metadata. (Security and Routing teams)
4) Postmortem: document in Confluence and update runbook to validate contract metadata during deployment and fallback testing.

Customer requested outcome:
- Refund/credit of the €18,564 charged during the fallback window, or an invoice re-issue reflecting the contractual fallback rate.
- Written assurance and a timeline for permanent fix.

Resolution notes (to be completed):
- 2026-03-12: Provisional credit created for the disputed amount and applied as a negative line on the March invoice (waiver id: WAIVE-2026-1147).
- Hotfix PR created for billing postback processor (https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/332).
- Security whitelist change scheduled for 2026-03-15.
- Customer notified and CSM coordinated next steps.
